thesis: A free, repeatable sacrifice outlet turns every body you control into three payments at once — a -1/-1 counter, a card, and one life off every seat — and the deck's real question is never how to go infinite but which of six kills the outlet is holding, because the three that ARE unbounded (stacks 009, 011, 012) need no commander and no counter, while the Nest of Scarabs line everyone names was measured by four passing stacks as a body-bounded rotation that grinds rather than wins.

stages.label: THIRTY-SIX LANDS AND A LIFE TOTAL
stages.what_it_does: Nineteen cards: 36 land copies across 16 entries (the two MDFCs are counted elsewhere), plus Sol Ring, Dark Ritual and Jet Medallion. 41 black sources against a 36-source target — five clear, and deck-audit's colour-sources axis reads AT, not short. The 33 that are lands are only part of the count: the target budgets SOURCES, not lands, and eight more come off nonland permanents. 76 black pips spread over 55 cards; mean available mana 5.23 at turn 6, land drop hit rate 58.9% there. FAST mana is only three cards — Sol Ring, Ancient Tomb, Dark Ritual — at 43.6% drawn / 34.8% by turn 6, the smallest and lowest-rated multi-card component the audit prices. The mana is engine-shaped, not acceleration-shaped, and the commander lands on mean turn 4.301 (median 4, 91% by turn 6) rather than turn 2. The second currency is LIFE. Ancient Tomb, City of Brass, Cabal Pit, Ifnir Deadlands and Castle Locthwain all charge it, every card in `fuel` charges it, and the outlet charges 1 per activation; the drains in `output` are the refund, which is why stack 011's loop ends with the pilot at 80. Four lands hold second jobs the mana count cannot see: Phyrexian Tower is a free outlet paying {B}{B}, Cabal Pit shrinks a creature, Takenuma buys a body back, Bojuka Bog exiles a graveyard. NOTHING IN THIS STAGE APPEARS IN A PASSING STACK — the eleven scenarios name Swamps as furniture and the citation index filters them, so every claim here is deterministic arithmetic, not verified board state.

evidence.note: THE WORKING LANDS is contained whole — all 16 entries — and the stage then adds three cards the map filed by what they say: Sol Ring in THE ON SWITCH, Dark Ritual in THE FUEL, and Jet Medallion in THE FODDER, which is a cost reducer sitting in the body pile
9 of 16 land entries carry land:utility, which is the taxonomy noticing the same thing the city gloss does: most of this mana holds a second job

stages.label: A FREE OUTLET, ON THE BATTLEFIELD
stages.what_it_does: Nine cards, and the first thing that has to happen. Nothing this deck holds is a resource until one of them is down: a body is only fodder if you can eat it at will, for no mana, at instant speed. Yawgmoth is the best of them — mana-free, instant-speed, and he pays a card back — and the other eight are 78.5% drawn / 68.0% by turn 6 — the third-deepest layer here, behind the nine-card drain layer and the nine-card RENEWABLE FODDER class at 82.3% each. TEN of the eleven presentable passing stacks open from a board where a sacrifice has ALREADY been paid, which is how load-bearing this stage is: it is assumed, not argued. Stack 006 is the one exception and it cuts the other way — Nest of Scarabs and three Swamps, no outlet anywhere on the board, a counter source making a body with nothing to eat it — which makes 006 the single verified support for the DECLARATION's reading of ignition. I still disagree with that reading. goldfish_targets names 'an ignition source drawn (something that places the first -1/-1 counter)' — eight cards, 73.8% — and that is the ignition of one BRANCH. The three unbounded kills are stacks 009, 011 and 012, and the string '-1/-1' appears nowhere in any of them; neither does Yawgmoth. Two exclude the branch outright by assumption: 012 says 'Nest of Scarabs is NOT on the battlefield' and 009 says 'no Nest of Scarabs, no Blowfly Infestation, no commander'. An outlet is on the board in all three. The counter is what the commander's branch converts; the outlet is what every branch needs. Price of running it: 1 life and one body per Yawgmoth activation, and the draw is MANDATORY — there is no 'may' — which is what bounds two of the six kills (010 and 014 both terminate on the library).

evidence.note: Phyrexian Altar's ability 'is a mana ability, so it never used the stack (605.3b)' — the outlet that also pays, and the loop it runs costs no life at all

the stack's own correction: Viscera Seer's free outlet is NOT a strictly favourable extra inside the Mikaeus loop, because only Yawgmoth's -1/-1 counter can strip the +1/+1 an undying return leaves behind. A second outlet is not always a second engine

THE ON SWITCH holds 7 of these 9 and its gloss — 'Nothing converts until one of these is down' — is the same reading this stage reaches from the stacks. The map and the engine AGREE here, which is rare. It disagrees twice: Woe Strider files under THE FODDER for its Goat and Warren Soultrader under THE FUEL for its Treasure, and the city also holds the five tutors and Sol Ring, which are `fuel` and `mana`

stages.label: BODIES THAT COME BACK
stages.what_it_does: Eleven cards: what the outlet eats, and what puts it back. Token engines that pay upkeep by upkeep (Bitterblossom, Ophiomancer, and Sedgemoor Witch off any instant or sorcery), a fat one-card board (Grave Titan), a body that recurs itself for {1}{B} (Reassembling Skeleton), and five ways to buy back a dead one — Animate Dead, Victimize, Persist, Agadeem's Awakening and Phyrexian Reclamation, the slow one because it returns to HAND rather than the battlefield — plus Stitcher's Supplier, which buys nothing back and mills three to fill the yard the other five draw from. Measured: mean bodies on board 4.239 at turn 6, and the audit's nine-card RENEWABLE FODDER class is 82.3% drawn / 72.2% by turn 6. That class is split across FOUR stages here on purpose, five of its nine landing in this one: Nest of Scarabs and Pawn of Ulamog make bodies only as the output of a death, so they are `conversion`; Gravecrawler is a kill half, so it is `wincon`; and Black Market Connections is bought for the cards, not the Demon, so it is `fuel`. THIS IS THE STAGE EVERY VERIFIED ROTATION RUNS OUT OF. Stacks 002, 003, 004 and 005 each end for the same reason and it is never life and never the library — it is bodies. 002 completes five activations from a three-body board; 005 gets eight because South Wind Avatar's 4 toughness absorbs four counters. One activation costs two bodies and returns one whenever the counter has to go on something of yours that dies to it, so the engine is body-NEGATIVE unless the deck keeps feeding it from here.

evidence.note: Persist returns Fume Spitter WITH a -1/-1 counter and CR 122.6 makes that count as YOU putting the counter on a creature — so a recursion spell is also a counter source, and the 0/0 it returns dies to state-based actions before the trigger even resolves
'the engine is bounded by bodies — each iteration costs two bodies and returns one, net minus one body per activation'; five completed activations, ended by having no other creature to sacrifice

10 of 11 sit in THE FODDER, which sounds like agreement and is not: that city holds 21 cards and this stage takes fewer than half of them, scattering the rest into `conversion` (Nest of Scarabs, Skullclamp), `wincon` (Gravecrawler, Butcher Ghoul, Mikaeus), `fuel` (Necropotence), `ignition` (Woe Strider) and `protection` (Lightning Greaves, Supernatural Stamina). A city named for bodies collects everything that mentions one

stages.label: CARDS, BOUGHT WITH LIFE
stages.what_it_does: Seven cards, and five of them are tutors. Necropotence and Black Market Connections print cards for life directly; Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor, Beseech the Mirror, Diabolic Intent and Insatiable Avarice convert one card into the exact missing half. The tutor class is 61.2% drawn / 50.3% by turn 6, and the goldfish models a drawn, affordable tutor as filling exactly ONE missing any_of group — that single substitution is the whole distance between the unassisted and assisted rates the rest of this file quotes: KILL E 13.5% → 58.8%, Gravecrawler 17.0% → 66.9%, the lone answer to a noncreature permanent 17.1% → 67.1%. Every tutor spent on defence is a tutor not spent on a kill half, and the simulation cannot model that choice. The bigger draw engine is not in this stage at all: it is the commander's own mandatory 'draw a card', and the goldfish's stated assumptions exclude extra card draw entirely, so every unassisted figure in this model is a FLOOR on games where Yawgmoth sticks and digs. No card in this stage appears in any of the eleven passing stacks — the verified tier covers 18 of the deck's 80 distinct cards and none of them is a tutor.

evidence.note: five copies, the whole assisted-rate mechanism, and the reason a 7.1% combo half is not the same fragility as a 7.1% deck

the five tutors are the one component in the scatter table that is 5-for-5 in a single city (THE ON SWITCH), and this stage still cuts across, because Necropotence sits in THE FODDER and Black Market Connections in THE FUEL — a city called THE FUEL that holds one of the seven cards this engine actually burns as fuel

stages.label: WHAT A DEATH BECOMES
stages.what_it_does: Seven cards, each turning a death into something that is NOT life loss: a token (Nest of Scarabs, Pawn of Ulamog), a Treasure (Pitiless Plunderer), two cards (Skullclamp, Deadly Dispute), one card per body sacrificed (Plumb the Forbidden), a sacrifice at every other seat (Grave Pact). Nest of Scarabs is the marquee — five of the eleven passing stacks name it, more than any card but the commander — and four of those five refute the line the card is famous for. From 002's three-body board the engine completes FIVE activations and stops on body exhaustion: seven deaths, 28 life off a pod of 160, pilot 39 → 42. 003 is the same board with Zulaport Cutthroat and settles that the pilot is never forced to eat his own drain (601.2h, 115.6). 004 is eight drains and its checker-passed resolution ends 'NOT A KILL, AND NOT EVEN CLOSE' — a verdict the adversarial checker did not merely accept: it 'wrote an exhaustive depth-first search over the whole move space' and reproduced every headline figure (8, 7, 28, 24) independently. 005 gets eight activations but only seven drains, because a body that dies at toughness 0 gains 0 life and CR 119.9 says that is not a lifegain event. 008 is the exception that pays double: Mirkwood Bats sees the sacrifice AND the creation, 13 triggers, each opponent 40 → 27. Rate for the declared kill built on this stage: 13.5% assembled / 58.8% assisted, mean turn 6.267. FOUR of the seven have no evidence at all — Grave Pact, Skullclamp, Deadly Dispute and Plumb the Forbidden are each absent from every passing stack, from every goldfish any_of and from all 39 contained lines. Only Nest of Scarabs, Pawn of Ulamog and Pitiless Plunderer carry any.

evidence.note: the sharpest refutation in the file: 'the engine ends by eating its own payoff' once Blood Artist is the last legal target. Eight drains, and the checker searched the line space exhaustively

one activation, TWO Mirkwood Bats triggers, and they never sit on the stack together — the sacrifice is a cost paid while the ability is already on the stack, the creation arrives two resolutions later
the bound is proved by case exhaustion over how the Avatar leaves the battlefield, and 'Spellbook's Near-infinite tag is wrong for this board'

three cities for seven cards: Nest of Scarabs and Skullclamp in THE FODDER, Pawn of Ulamog / Pitiless Plunderer / Deadly Dispute in THE FUEL, Grave Pact and Plumb the Forbidden in THE DEATH TAX. The stage is defined by an EVENT its members do not describe — they describe the by-product, and the map files each one under its by-product

stages.label: TWO PRODUCTS, ONE CURRENCY
stages.what_it_does: Sixteen cards, and the two halves are the same currency rather than two suites. The DRAIN half is nine deep — Bastion of Remembrance, Zulaport Cutthroat, Blood Artist, Mirkwood Bats, Ayara, South Wind Avatar, Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric, The Meathook Massacre — at 82.3% drawn / 72.0% by turn 6, the deck's best-built layer; Gray Merchant is the tenth, a one-shot version of the same text. That nine-card rate is NOT every kill's drain rate, and the split is functional: only KILL E and KILL F draw their drain slot from all nine. KILL A, B and D need a DEATH-triggered drain and take a 3-deep group (Bastion, Zulaport, Ayara); KILL C needs a LIFEGAIN-triggered one and takes a disjoint 3-deep group (South Wind Avatar, Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric). Four of the six kills have a three-card drain layer, not a nine-card one. Bastion of Remembrance alone is named in four passing stacks (002, 009, 010, 011). The SUBTRACTION half — Fume Spitter, Skinrender, Soul Snuffers, Black Sun's Zenith, Massacre Girl's wither, Sinister Gnarlbark's blight — is not a second removal suite: a -1/-1 counter placed on anything is a Nest of Scarabs trigger and a shrunken creature is still a body the outlet can eat, so the deck's removal and the deck's engine spend the same resource. Spot removal aimed at a permanent that is a PROBLEM — Fatal Push, Deadly Rollick, Feed the Swarm — lives in `protection` instead, because it answers the table rather than feeding the engine. Both halves feed backwards: the drains refund the life the outlet spends, and 002 measures the refund exactly — five activations against seven death triggers, ending 39 → 42, the board having arrived at 39 with the first activation's life already paid, so the ledger closes as 39 − 4 + 7.

evidence.note: six of the seven drains are TOKEN deaths and they count: 704.5f puts the 0/0 token in the graveyard and 704.5d removes it only on the NEXT state-based-action check, so it dies first and ceases to exist second
the life ledger: five activations against seven Bastion triggers, pilot 39 → 42 (the board was handed over at 39 with the first activation's life already paid) while each opponent goes 40 → 33

THE DEATH TAX holds nine of these and THE SUBTRACTION five, with Ayara in THE ON SWITCH and Massacre Girl in THE FODDER. The map splits the deck's two products into two cities because one set says 'each opponent loses 1 life' and the other says 'put a -1/-1 counter'; the engine spends them as one thing

stages.label: INSURANCE, AND ONE ANSWER
stages.what_it_does: Six cards. Lightning Greaves puts shroud on a commander whose entire job is standing on the battlefield being activated. Malakir Rebirth and Supernatural Stamina answer a removal spell by letting the creature die and come straight back — and the death still pays every drain, which is the shape this deck wants from insurance. Deadly Rollick is free while you control a commander, Fatal Push kills the cheap thing, and Feed the Swarm is the card the audit prices as this stage's single point of failure: the deck's only answer to a noncreature permanent, 17.1% drawn / 67.1% if a tutor is spent on defence instead of a kill half. READ THAT FIGURE NARROWLY. Feed the Swarm destroys 'target creature or enchantment an opponent controls' — it cannot touch an artifact — and the format's cheap hosers for THIS deck are artifacts: Grafdigger's Cage on the graveyard casting and the undying returns, Cursed Totem on every creature outlet including the commander. The odds of answering either are not 17.1%; they are zero. The interaction axis reads 2 of 5 classes (creature 14, enchantment 1, artifact 0, graveyard 0, land 0), and no card among the 80 destroys, exiles or bounces an artifact. What binds here is therefore not a draw rate on one enchantment answer — it is a class covered zero times, which no draw improves. Nothing in this stage appears in any passing stack, so none of it is verified in play; it is the layer the eleven scenarios assume away when they state 'no player responds to anything'.

evidence.note: three copies, and the one that can leave the creature type — Feed the Swarm — reaches only enchantments, so the noncreature answer is enchantment-wide, not permanent-wide

three cities for six cards: the answers sit in THE SUBTRACTION beside the five -1/-1 sweepers this model calls `output`, while the two dies-and-returns tricks are filed as recursion in THE FODDER and THE FUEL. The map cannot tell an answer from an engine part when both are written as 'target creature'

stages.label: SIX KILLS, FIVE HALVES
stages.what_it_does: Five cards, each the named half of a declared kill: Gravecrawler (KILL A and KILL B), Exquisite Blood (C), Mikaeus (D), Butcher Ghoul with Geralf's Messenger (F). Three of the six kills are genuinely unbounded and all three are checker-verified. 009: Warren Soultrader plus Gravecrawler plus a drain — each iteration's Treasure exactly funds the next cast, 39 further iterations put all four opponents at 0 at once. 011: Phyrexian Altar instead, and it costs no life at all — the pilot ends at 80. 012: Exquisite Blood plus a you-gain-they-lose body, mandatory, and the checker settled that it is a win and not the CR 104.4b draw because every iteration lowers every opponent's life. The other two are library-bounded and still lethal: 010 needs 39 more activations against the 59 the library permits, 014 kills at ~30 activations inside a ~55 bound with ~25 draws of margin. The rules are not the problem — the rates are. A 1.3% / 18.2% assisted, B 0.6% / 12.0%, C 6.6% / 42.6%, D 4.6% / 34.3%, F 1.8% / 26.9%. The best-drawing line is KILL E at 13.5% / 58.8%, and four passing stacks say its board grinds rather than wins, which is why the card that names it sits in `conversion` and not here.

evidence.note: 'The loop is self-funding and unbounded; 40 drain events bring a seat to exactly 0 — one has already resolved, so 39 further iterations take all four opponents to 0 at once'

'not one that could be repeated indefinitely (732.1b) and there is a way to stop (104.4b)' — the mandatory loop is a win, not a draw, and it needs no outlet: Carrion Feeder's ability at pos 0 never resolves
'unbounded is the wrong word' — the mandatory draw caps it at ~55 activations, and lethality at ~30 arrives with ~25 draws to spare

the highest-popularity contained line in the deck (60,592) and one of 11 two-card infinites among 39 contained lines. EIGHT of the 39 have every one of their cards inside a single checker-passed stack — this one is 011's, and two of the other seven are my own other unbounded kills, 009's and 012's. That count is a set intersection of candidate_lines[].cards with verified.by_card, so it is mechanically checkable rather than a reading

three of the five (Gravecrawler, Butcher Ghoul, Mikaeus) are filed in THE FODDER because their text describes a creature, and two (Exquisite Blood, Geralf's Messenger) in THE DEATH TAX because their text says 'loses life'. Nothing in either city marks them as halves of five DIFFERENT kills, which is the only property that matters about them

lines.note: DASHED ON PURPOSE. The turn-2 commander needs the three-card fast-mana class (43.6% drawn / 34.8% by turn 6) and no passing stack shows a ritual paying for him. He is on SEVEN of the eleven (002, 003, 004, 005, 008, 010, 014) and each of those seven begins with him already resolved; the other four — 006, 009, 011, 012 — hold no commander at all, which is the thesis. Measured reality is slower: mean cast turn 4.301, median 4, 91% by turn 6.

DASHED, and it is the deck's most basic flow. Not one of the eleven passing stacks puts a token engine on the table next to an outlet: ten open with the sacrifice already paid, and the eleventh (006) has no outlet on the board at all. So the arrow the whole deck rests on is the one with no stack behind it. Mean bodies at turn 6 is 4.239.

One activation is 1 life plus a body, and it buys a counter, a card, and one Insect back. Body-neutral only while the counter lands on something that survives it or is not yours; on 002's board that is one 2/2, and after it dies every legal target is your own 1/1.

Seven creature deaths, seven Bastion triggers, 28 life off a pod of 160 — five sacrificed and two counter-killed. The rotation is real and it is finite: 'the lowest life total on the table is 33', so nothing dies.

The one drain that gets paid twice per activation, because Bats reads 'create OR sacrifice a token' and one activation supplies both. Thirteen triggers on the 003 board class, each opponent 40 → 27 — more than either sibling engine, and the counter-killed Insects pay only on creation.

THE FEEDBACK LOOP. Yawgmoth charges 1 life an activation and the drain refunds 1 a death; on 002's board five activations meet seven death triggers and the pilot ends 39 → 42 — the board arrived at 39 with the first activation's life already paid, so the ledger is 39 − 4 + 7 rather than 39 − 5 + 7. This is why a deck that pays life on nine other cards can keep paying: the engine is life-positive whenever the drain is down.

Two mana buys a body, a counter and a death at once: Persist returns Fume Spitter WITH a -1/-1 counter, CR 122.6 makes that count as YOU placing it, and the 0/0 dies to state-based actions before the trigger resolves. The Nest of Scarabs on that board is filtered out of the citation index (the stack and graveyard name the line, so the board is skipped), so this arrow claims only what the two named cards do.

DASHED, AND THE BIGGEST UNDECLARED THING IN THE DECK. With Ashnod's Altar (in `ignition`) these three are a fully contained bracket-1 line: sacrifice the Skeleton for {C}{C} and a Treasure, return it for {1}{B} paid with a {C} and that Treasure, net +{C} and one death per cycle. SEVEN of the nine drains would convert that into a kill — Bastion, Zulaport, Blood Artist one seat at a time, Mirkwood Bats off the Treasure created and sacrificed, Ayara off the black Skeleton re-entering, South Wind Avatar, The Meathook Massacre. The other two do not: Marauding Blight-Priest and Starscape Cleric trigger only on YOU gaining life, and this loop gains none, so with either as the sole drain it runs forever and removes nothing. And the conditional is the point — it is in candidate_lines, in no goldfish target, and no stack has resolved it, on a deck where 005 refuted a Spellbook 'Near-infinite' tag outright and 001 did something narrower — it CONFIRMED the 'Infinite' tag on Blowfly Infestation plus Nest of Scarabs ('genuinely unbounded') and refuted it as a KILL, 3 per opponent rather than 40. 001 is non-presentable, so that precedent can be argued in prose and can never be a verified_by.

DASHED. The five tutors are how the kills actually arrive: one tutor is modelled as filling exactly one missing group, which moves Gravecrawler from 17.0% to 66.9% and KILL E from 13.5% to 58.8%. Spend it on Feed the Swarm instead and both numbers revert.

KILL A. Gravecrawler's own ability modifies which zone it can be cast from (113.6f) and Soultrader is the Zombie that turns the permission on and is never sacrificed ('another creature'). Each iteration's Treasure exactly funds the next {B}: self-funding, unbounded, and exactly one drain per iteration, because only Gravecrawler's death matches Bastion's trigger event — 009's own words, 'neither creating nor sacrificing a Treasure adds drain (603.2)'.

KILL B, and it is free rather than merely self-funding: no life is paid at any point, the pilot GAINS 1 a cycle and ends at 80. The Altar's ability is a mana ability that never uses the stack (605.3b) and Carrion Feeder is the second Zombie, never eaten.

Exactly one drain per iteration, and 011 gives its own reason rather than 009's: cards.json gives Bastion TWO triggered abilities, and only the death trigger can fire in this loop because Bastion never re-enters, so nothing fires when Gravecrawler returns (603.2). No figure is imported from 009 — 011's board is Carrion Feeder, not Warren Soultrader, and holds no Treasure at all; the mana comes from Phyrexian Altar. Forty drain events per seat; one has resolved, so 39 further iterations kill all four seats at the same state-based-action check.

KILL D. The -1/-1 counter is a RESET, not a shrink: 704.5q removes one +1/+1 and one -1/-1 simultaneously, leaving Gravecrawler at zero counters and alive, so undying re-arms it for the next death. Library-bounded — 39 more activations needed against the 59 the mandatory draw permits.

KILL F, three opponents in this scenario rather than four. Per two-activation cycle each opponent loses 2 to Zulaport and the Messenger's chosen seat loses 4 IN TOTAL — its 2 from Zulaport plus 2 from the Messenger's enters trigger — so across the three seats the pod total is 8, and the pilot is net 0 life and 2 cards. The counter-stripping is the mechanism: a body that dies holding a +1/+1 fails undying's intervening 'if' and never triggers.

KILL C, the only kill needing no commander and no recursion — and drawn as a backward arrow because it IS a loop: the Avatar drains, the Blood gains it back, the gain drains again. It does need a SEED: 012's board holds Carrion Feeder and Insect token X was sacrificed to it to pay the cost of the ability on the stack, which is the death that gave the Avatar its 1 life. What 012 establishes is that once any lifegain seeds it the alternation is self-sustaining and needs no outlet to CONTINUE. One drain per cycle, drain #40 takes all four seats to 0 at the same check, and the pilot ends at 80. Fastest-assembling kill by mean turn (5.085).

map_disagreements.component: An ignition source drawn (something that places the first -1/-1 counter)
map_disagreements.why: Eight cards, four cities, 4/2/1/1 — the worst scatter in the table. The class is defined by an EVENT (a -1/-1 counter arriving on a creature) and its members describe four unrelated things: 'destroy target creature', 'put three -1/-1 counters', 'return target card from your graveyard', 'each creature gets -X/-X'. No member says it is an ignition source, so the map files each one by its by-product. This model also disagrees with the component's NAME: three of the deck's six kills (stacks 009, 011, 012) place no -1/-1 counter anywhere and hold no Yawgmoth either, so BOTH halves of the declared class are absent from every unbounded kill. This class ignites one branch, not the engine.

map_disagreements.component: A free repeatable sacrifice outlet drawn (not counting Yawgmoth)
map_disagreements.why: Eight cards, 6/1/1, and the two strays are the informative part. Woe Strider files under THE FODDER because its text makes a Goat, and Warren Soultrader under THE FUEL because its text makes a Treasure — both are free repeatable outlets and the map read the by-product instead of the ability. This is the one component where the city NAME is right: THE ON SWITCH's gloss, 'Nothing converts until one of these is down', is the same finding this model's `ignition` stage reaches from the eleven stacks.

map_disagreements.component: ENGINE MANA drawn — turns a creature death into castable black
map_disagreements.why: Five cards, three cities. The class is one sentence — a death becomes castable black — and the map cannot see it because Phyrexian Tower is typed as a land, Phyrexian Altar reads as a sacrifice outlet, and Warren Soultrader reads as ramp. This is what makes stack 011's loop free rather than merely repeatable, and it is invisible on the map by construction.

map_disagreements.component: The five kill halves (this model's `wincon` stage)
map_disagreements.why: Three of the five (Gravecrawler, Butcher Ghoul, Mikaeus) are filed in THE FODDER because their oracle text is about creatures, and two (Exquisite Blood, Geralf's Messenger) in THE DEATH TAX because theirs says 'loses life'. Both filings are correct readings of the cards and neither can express the property that matters — that these are the named halves of five DIFFERENT kills, three of them unbounded, with assembly rates spanning 0.6% to 6.6% unassisted.

A single-card disagreement worth naming because it shows the mechanism cleanly: a two-mana cost reducer sits in the city of bodies. It says nothing about creatures and does nothing with deaths; it belongs with the mana, and the layout put it next to the thing it happens to be cheapest alongside.

open_questions.question: Does Ashnod's Altar + Pitiless Plunderer + Reassembling Skeleton hold as an unbounded line on a real board? Commander Spellbook rates it bracket 1 for infinite colorless mana and infinite death triggers, all three cards are in the 99, and the arithmetic looks self-funding (sacrifice for {C}{C} plus a Treasure, recur for {1}{B}), but nothing has resolved it and neither Plunderer nor the Skeleton appears in any of the eleven passing stacks.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would be the deck's fourth unbounded kill and the first that needs neither the commander nor Gravecrawler — which is to say it would retire the single point of failure the `wincon` stage currently carries at 17.0% drawn.

open_questions.question: Does Mikaeus, the Unhallowed plus ONE free sacrifice outlet loop without the commander? Seven such pairings are in candidate_lines (Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Woe Strider, Yahenni, Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Blasting Station) and all seven outlets are in the 99, but undying's intervening 'if' fails the moment the body carries a +1/+1 counter — which is exactly what stack 010 needed Yawgmoth's -1/-1 counter to strip.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the pairings are wrong, seven candidate lines are noise for this deck and KILL D is correctly declared as commander-gated; if any is right, the deck holds a two-card kill that does not deck you, and KILL D's declaration understates it.

open_questions.question: How many Nest of Scarabs rotations, across how many turns, does an average board actually need to kill a four-opponent pod? Stacks 002/003/004/005 each measure exactly ONE rotation from a three-body board — 5 to 8 activations, 7 to 13 drains, 28 to 52 life removed from 160 — and none of them carries the board into a second turn.
open_questions.why_it_matters: KILL E's 13.5% / 58.8% is the deck's headline number and it prices assembling a line that four checker-passed stacks say does not win on the spot.
